Cases.Name: Policy defaults are opt-in and reject invalid bounds
Backup scheduling respects interval, busy state and failed-attempt cooldown
Move copies and verifies then redirects the preserved original
Restart discovers durable operation without writing and explicit resume verifies it
Rollback removes only its own marker before any new target commit
An intervening source write or preexisting destination refuses the copy
Rollback refuses a target that received a later commit
Restore uses a separate verified target and never overwrites the active file
Backup is standalone and readable after export without WAL sidecars
Complete backup restores canonical data queries and the hash-linked preferences snapshot
Mismatched or over-deep preferences are refused before a restore changes its active base
Changing only the preferences attachment invalidates a confirmed restore preview
Migration backup preserves pre-change schema and survives regular backup rotation
Retention deletes only old migrated families and preserves unknown recent and legacy rows
Retention with no eligible rows avoids a redundant backup and preserves the revision
Retention refusal rolls back and never silently accepts stale confirmation

Point 36: unreadable patterns are the same in the model and the maintenance worker
Point 36: the integrity worker checks exactly the tables and columns of the model
Point 36: integrity check of a healthy base is read-only and clean
Point 36: integrity check reports foreign identity, newer receipts and missing columns
Point 36: integrity check of an unreadable file reports it without throwing
